clue.text: One bellyaching about daft mare's death

indicators.note: the complainer's letters are placed around the other piece

parts.note: a griper is someone who complains or bellyaches

indicators.note: daft means crazy, so the letters of the horse are jumbled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A grumbler moans about a silly horse dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daft' makes the horse's letters MREA, and 'about' wraps the complainer round them. The 's of mare's is no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The personified figure of death with a scythe is called this.

clue.text: Bird raised plant, needing a lot of water

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are read upwards, i.e. backwards
only most of the tree's name is wanted, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: an acacia is a tree or shrub

explanation.surface: A bird lifts a plant that needs lots of watering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing a lot of' cuts ACACIA to ACACI, and 'raised' turns that to ICACA. 'Needing' looks like the link to the definition, but it belongs to the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Titicaca in the Andes is a vast freshwater lake, a large body of water.

clue.text: What gardener does to mature plant's humble dwelling?

definitions.text: What gardener does to mature plant
definitions.meaning: a gardener moves a grown plant into a bed
a single rented room used for living and sleeping

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as two words and it is what a gardener does to a plant that is ready: 'beds it'. The 's joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsitter is a one-room rented flat, the most modest kind of home.

clue.text: Slight incline

definitions.meaning: slight here means slim or thin
to incline is to tilt or slope

explanation.definitionFit: Thin people are described as lean, and to tilt to one side is to lean.

clue.text: Perform sex act on prisoner in bondage, as dominatrix may

indicators.note: the prisoner is held tied up inside the other word

parts.note: to fellate is to perform oral sex
a lag is a convict, especially an old lag

explanation.surface: A racy instruction about kinky treatment of a captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bondage' signals the prisoner held inside the verb; 'on' is a link. The definition is the whole closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A dominatrix may whip her client, and to whip someone is to flog or scourge them.

clue.text: Have songwriter up for having dates

parts.note: to 'have up for' someone is to put them on trial, so this means try
Sting is the English singer-songwriter, formerly of the Police

explanation.surface: A songwriter is taken to court over going out with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have ... up for' means to put on trial, as in 'had up for speeding', but the songwriter's name sits in the middle of that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a lovers' meeting, so keeping trysts means going on dates.

clue.text: Island that's upholding another one

indicators.note: the turned word holds the next piece inside it
in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the word is turned around

parts.note: the word that is taken as written; the 's links it to the rest
another one, i.e. a second I for one
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One island is said to support another.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'upholding' as 'up holding': 'up' turns THAT to TAHT, and 'holding' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island in French Polynesia.

clue.text: Time to show affection for hoodie, perhaps?

parts.note: to hug is to embrace someone fondly

explanation.surface: Hugging a hoodie-wearing youth, as a politician once suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'hug a hoodie' phrase from British politics in 2006 makes the hoodie sound loveable. Here a hoodie is a young lout in a hooded top.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodie, a youth in a hooded top, is stereotyped as a hooligan or ruffian.

clue.text: Cause trouble with high heels, boarding type of transport

indicators.note: the jumbled letters get on board, i.e. go inside

parts.note: rail is a means of transport

indicators.note: high as in drunk or intoxicated, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone in stilettos boards a train and makes a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like part of 'high heels' but it is the anagram signal, making SEHEL; 'boarding' puts that inside the transport word.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick up a fuss or make a great commotion is an idiom with this meaning.

clue.text: Inhabitant of water butt

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish of the carp family
the stub of a cannabis cigarette

explanation.walkthrough: A water butt is a rain barrel, but the two words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish lives in rivers, and the slang term names the end of a joint.

clue.text: O' ___ men, as Burns almost said in "Chinatown"?

indicators.note: the phrase in the poem sounds nearly like the town's name when spoken

parts.note: Burns wrote 'The best laid schemes o' mice an' men'; the gap is the bit before 'men'

explanation.surface: A gap in a quotation from Robert Burns, set in a film title.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns's poem To a Mouse has 'o' mice an' men'; 'mice an'' said aloud is close to the town. Chinatown is the film, but here it means a town famous for china.
explanation.definitionFit: Meissen in Saxony is famous for the porcelain made there, so it is a china town.

clue.text: Try to chuck Little Bird

parts.note: to have a go is to try
to sling is to throw or chuck

explanation.surface: An attempt to throw a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A young goose is a small bird not yet grown.

clue.text: European treaty establishing discrepancy between calendars

parts.note: a pact is a formal agreement or treaty

explanation.surface: A European agreement settles differences in dating systems.
explanation.definitionFit: The epact is the number of days by which the solar year exceeds the lunar year.

clue.text: Bordeaux, say, is in peace with orthodoxy

indicators.note: the wine and the next word go inside the word for peace

parts.note: calm is peace and quiet
Bordeaux is an example of wine, French vin
taken as written

explanation.surface: A glass of claret brings quiet and conformity.
explanation.walkthrough: VIN is French for wine, and Bordeaux is a French wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Protestant doctrine of John Calvin became a strict orthodoxy in Geneva and Scotland.

clue.text: University fees take the "Liberal" out of party leader — which is not all bad

indicators.note: the shortened name takes in the other pieces
the L is removed from the leader's name

parts.note: Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats when this puzzle appeared
rates are charges or fees

explanation.surface: Political gibe about student fees and a Lib Dem leader shedding his liberalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' puts the university and fees pieces inside CEGG, left when the Liberal goes 'out of' the leader's name. Nick Clegg led Britain's Liberal Democrats in 2010.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something with good and bad parts, from a curate politely calling a bad egg good in parts.

clue.text: Bloody compiler! Lousy, keeping union member up

parts.note: the setter of a crossword refers to himself as me

indicators.note: the word for lousy keeps the other pieces inside it

parts.note: dire means very bad or lousy

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: an arm is a limb or member

explanation.surface: An exasperated outburst about a bad setter and a trade union member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the limb to MRA; 'keeping' puts UMRA inside the word for lousy. 'Bloody' looks like an oath at the setter but is how a steak is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak cooked this way is still pink and bloody inside.

clue.text: Head of state's minders ordered to do eg "Ra-Ra-Rasputin" without head of state

indicators.note: the letters are put in order anew, i.e. rearranged
a letter is removed from the song title
the first letter of the word state

explanation.surface: Bodyguards are ordered to perform a disco hit about a Russian mystic.
explanation.walkthrough: Ra-Ra-Rasputin is the Boney M disco hit. 'without' drops S, the 'head of state', leaving RARARAPUTIN; 'ordered' rearranges that with DOEG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Praetorian Guard were the bodyguards of the Roman emperors.

clue.text: Music maker's sort of disc cutting sort of steak

indicators.note: the disc cuts into the steak, going inside it

parts.note: a T-bone is a cut of beef steak
ROM, as in CD-ROM, is a kind of disc

explanation.surface: A disc slicing through a steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts the disc type inside the steak; the 's of maker's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass instrument with a slide is a maker of music.

clue.text: Reverse decision to encase small sibling in mineral

indicators.note: to encase one thing in another is to put it inside
the sibling goes in the mineral

parts.note: agate is a banded form of quartz
bro is short for brother

explanation.surface: Changing one's mind about sealing a little brother in stone.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrogate a law or agreement is to repeal or annul it, undoing an earlier decision.

clue.text: Formerly meeting sticky ends — those of Emperor Trajan, Nero, etc?

indicators.note: a sticky end is a bad one, so the letters meet a messy fate and are rearranged
the last letters of the two words named

explanation.surface: Roman emperors who came to sticky ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters R and N, from 'ends — those of', go with NEROETC; 'sticky' rearranges the lot. Formerly flags an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word, from French, for an encounter or meeting.

clue.text: Spoon about to be dropped by fool

indicators.note: the abbreviation is removed from the longer word

parts.note: to spoon is to canoodle, kiss and cuddle
CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A spoon is discarded by a silly person.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoon is the old verb for courting, not the cutlery.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is an old-fashioned word for a simpleton.

clue.text: Island going west in "Prufrock"

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means read right to left
the letters are found within the word

explanation.surface: An island turns up in T S Eliot's poem about Prufrock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks out UFROC inside the word, and 'going west' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea.

clue.text: Frank has the ability — and proved it

parts.note: can means is able to
did, as in 'she said she would and she did'

explanation.surface: Frank is capable and showed it.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means open and honest, saying what one thinks.

clue.text: Sun exposes party leader taking weed on public vehicle

indicators.note: the first letter of the word party

parts.note: to hoe is to clear weeds
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: A newspaper exposé of a politician gardening on a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is the British tabloid newspaper in the surface, and it is the definition in the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoebus is a name of Apollo as sun god, used poetically for the sun.

clue.text: Less than mature mammal on top of a less than mature insect

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a pup is a young dog or seal

explanation.surface: A young animal riding on a young insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupa is the chrysalis stage of an insect, before it becomes an adult.

clue.text: Trough engulfing a boss

indicators.note: the trough swallows the letter inside it

parts.note: a manger is a feeding trough

explanation.surface: An animal trough swallowing a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager is the person in charge, the boss.

clue.text: Drink and drug necked by loony

indicators.note: necked means swallowed, so the drug goes inside the word

parts.note: mad means crazy or loony
E is slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A lunatic downs a drink and a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'necked by' puts E inside MAD. Necking a drink is British slang for gulping it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an alcoholic drink made from honey.

clue.text: Politician who's into huntin' 'n' fencin'?

definitions.meaning: Sarah ..., the American politician known for hunting
paling fencing with its final G dropped, as in huntin'

explanation.walkthrough: The dropped G of huntin' and fencin' tells you to drop the G of paling, a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Palin hunts moose, and paling means fencing with the last letter missing.

clue.text: Fighter's pleased a riot's erupted

parts.note: glad means pleased

indicators.note: erupted means burst out, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A fighter is happy a riot has broken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erupted' rearranges ARIOT to IATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator fought in the Roman arena.
